speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin my evaluation of your postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness, could you please tell me how many days have passed since your delivery? Additionally, have you noticed any abnormal vaginal discharge or odor?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. I'd like to check your vital signs and examine your abdomen for any rigidity or rebound tenderness, which could indicate peritonitis or another serious complication. Are you experiencing any pain during urination or have you noticed any blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the uterine tenderness, fever, and history of prolonged labor with a large infant, endometritis is the primary concern, but we must rule out a urinary tract infection or pelvic abscess. I will order a Complete Blood Count and a Urinalysis to check for infection markers and white blood cells in the urine. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Urinalysis
